description: The hand-verified expected result for the CAPTURED positive Dependency-Check fixture, oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/captured-dependency-check-vulnerabilities.json. This fixture exists because the scanning run's own Dependency-Check artifact contains zero vulnerability records and therefore cannot exercise one positive field; this one is genuine, unmodified output of the same tool build over different input, and it exercises the twelve-field positive mapping end to end.

fixture.lines_convention: logical lines: len(text.splitlines()), which counts a final line that carries no trailing newline
fixture.provenance: AN UNMODIFIED CAPTURE of genuine tool output, taken whole rather than as an excerpt. It is the complete JSON report of a second Dependency-Check invocation, recorded with its exact command, tool build, JDK, feed timestamps and measured output in harness/artifacts/logs/dependency-check-positive-capture.log. Nothing in it is authored, reordered, truncated or reformatted; the test corpus asserts byte equality against the retained report rather than against a digest this tree owns.
fixture.why_a_second_invocation: harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json -- the whole of this tool's output for the scanning run -- carries 32 dependencies, zero vulnerability records and zero package objects, because exactly one manifest-shaped file is in scanned scope (AAP 0.2.1). One vulnerability record is this shape's count unit, so no excerpt of that artifact can exercise any positive field. Widening the twelve globs is prohibited (AAP 0.3.2) and relabelling authored data as a capture is prohibited, so the tool was run again, unchanged, over input that resolves to packages the seeded feed carries advisories for.
fixture.not_part_of_the_scanning_run: This invocation wrote outside harness/artifacts/raw/, was not normalized, and contributes no row to findings.json or findings.csv. The dependency-check entry in tool-status.md still reports zero rows, and that remains a true statement about the scanned scope.

resolution_context.root_derivation: The capture's own scan root, derived from the fixture itself: the common parent directory of the captured dependencies' filePath values. Deriving it from the document keeps this expectation portable -- no host path is recorded here and none is needed, because the adapter relativizes lexically.
resolution_context.path_base_source: the same base the dependency-check entry of harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json records: this tool writes filePath as a filesystem-absolute path
resolution_context.allowlist: the twelve globs; no glob covers the Maven local repository, so every row is out of scope

absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv.

captured_positive_mapping.requirement: AAP 0.6.2 and AAP 0.9.4: an unmodified captured positive fixture per adapter, exercising that adapter's positive field mapping, with a hand-verified expected result asserted field by field.
captured_positive_mapping.statement: SATISFIED by genuine captured tool output. Five vulnerability records over two dependencies exercise rule_id, message, severity_native with three distinct labels, severity_norm through the label-over-score precedence, filesystem-absolute path relativization, cve, cwe including the ascending-numeric-identifier rule over a record that lists the larger identifier first, and package_coordinate at candidate level 2 of the four-level precedence. start_line is absent because the record shape carries no line, and in_scope is false because the scanned input lies outside the twelve globs -- both stated rather than glossed.

fields_this_fixture_does_not_exercise.behaviour: a vulnerability whose severity is absent, so severity_norm falls to the CVSS score
package-coordinate candidate levels 1, 3 and 4 and the within-level lexicographic tie
every rejection condition this adapter can produce
fields_this_fixture_does_not_exercise.cover_with: the reject-dependency-check-* fixtures, one per condition

rows.message: Serialized-object interfaces in certain Cisco Collaboration and Social Media; Endpoint Clients and Client Software; Network Application, Service, and Acceleration; Network and Content Security Devices; Network Management and Provisioning; Routing and Switching - Enterprise and Service Provider; Unified Computing; Voice and Unified Communications Devices; Video, Streaming, TelePresence, and Transcoding Devices; Wireless; and Cisco Hosted Services products allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via a crafted serialized Java object, related to the Apache Commons Collections (ACC) library.

jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, jackson-databind's PolymorphicTypeValidator (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains <), DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() validates only the raw container class name (the substring before <) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical() and returns the fully parameterized type without ever validating the nested type arguments against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore place a denied class as a generic type parameter of an allowed container — for example java.util.ArrayList<com.evil.Gadget> when only java.util.ArrayList is allow-listed. The container passes the PTV check; com.evil.Gadget is loaded via Class.forName(name, true, loader), instantiated, and its properties are set from attacker-controlled JSON. This completely bypasses an explicitly configured PTV allow-list. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder.allowIfSubTypeIsArray() allowlists any array type based only on clazz.isArray(), without validating the array's component (element) type against the configured allowlist. A PTV built with allowIfSubTypeIsArray() plus an explicit concrete-type allowlist therefore still permits EvilType[] even though EvilType is not allowlisted. When Jackson deserializes the elements and no per-element type IDs are present, it instantiates the component type directly with no further PTV check, bypassing the allowlist. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.0.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, JDKFromStringDeserializer constructed InetSocketAddress with new InetSocketAddress(host, port), which performs eager DNS name resolution for hostname inputs at deserialization time. An application that binds untrusted JSON into a type containing an InetSocketAddress field issues an attacker-chosen DNS query during readValue, before any application-level validation or connect logic. The fix uses InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved(host, port), deferring DNS to an explicit connect. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.8.0 until 2.18.9, 2.21.5, and 3.1.4, in BeanDeserializerBase.createContextual(), per-property @JsonIgnoreProperties exclusions are applied by _handleByNameInclusion(), producing a contextual deserializer whose BeanPropertyMap has the ignored properties removed. The subsequent per-property case-insensitivity block (triggered by @JsonFormat(ACCEPT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_PROPERTIES)) rebuilds from this._beanProperties (the original, unfiltered map) instead of contextual._beanProperties, then overwrites the filtered map — restoring every property _handleByNameInclusion had just removed. The ignored property becomes writable again. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.9, 2.21.5, and 3.1.4.

row_derivations.severity_precedence_applied: The native label governs and the CVSS score is not consulted. This record also carries CVSS baseScore(s) [9.8], which is recorded to show the precedence is exercised rather than vacuous: the label decides.
